decisions.reason: The approved Hero V remains the unchanged source geometry; the client reopens only the second V.
The existing exploration boundary incorrectly requires the second V to remain locked, while this source explicitly reopens it for two controlled options before alphabet refinement continues.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Thank you for restoring the foundation. I think we're much closer now.

Before we continue refining the alphabet, I'd like to revisit one aspect of the VvÉ system. Looking back at our earlier explorations, I prefer the hierarchy between the Hero V and the second V in concepts #2 and #3 (attached). I don't think the current proof has quite achieved that same relationship yet.

Will you please show these two options?

Option 1: Create the second V by copying the approved Hero V and reducing it proportionally as a single object (without redrawing it). It should remain a true scaled version of the Hero V while still extending above the E and L.

Option 2: Start with that same copied-and-scaled Hero V, then make only the minimal optical refinements you feel are necessary so it integrates more naturally with the alphabet while preserving the same identity and maintaining its elevation above the E and L.

Next, will you please refine the optical spacing throughout the word? I like the visual rhythm of the L–V relationship in this proof and would use that as the benchmark for balancing the remaining letter pairs.

I've attached the earlier concepts as a reference for the Hero V/second V relationship I'm referring to.

Thank you!

value_updates.exploration_boundary: Explore the E and L around the locked Hero V and É accent while evaluating the second V under the two explicitly requested copied-and-scaled options.

decisions.reason: Both requested second-V options begin with the complete copied-and-scaled Hero V, necessarily carrying its terminal gesture into the second V and superseding the prior rule excluding propagation to that glyph.
